turns.assessment: The event is an optical, multi-channel failure: numerous line receivers lost optical power and OSNR simultaneously, while many services switched protection. A client-port, OTN-switch, or individual transponder fault cannot explain that scope. Unchanged amplifier and OMS telemetry argues strongly against a fibre cut, pulled connector, or pump failure on the common spans; the pattern instead fits a degree-selective WSS input-port failure at the shared S19 ROADM, with the recent S19 maintenance adding supporting evidence.

proposals.rationale: A failed WSS input port at roadm.S19 can simultaneously block all channels arriving on one degree while leaving other degrees and upstream optical plant normal. This explains the widespread OCH LOS, lost receiver power, downstream channel-power losses, and mixed affected/unaffected services. The absence of changes on common amplifiers and spans weighs against a plant break, and S19 had recent maintenance.

A degree-selective WSS port failure at roadm.S08 could also explain why many services through S08 failed while services using other S08 degrees remained operational. It is less likely because the broader optical propagation pattern and recent maintenance favor S19.

clarify.assessment: The evidence localizes the committed WSS_PORT_FAIL to roadm.S19, but it does not map the affected lightpaths to a specific S19 ingress degree. Normal upstream monitoring on the listed incoming OMSs is consistent with a WSS input-port failure and does not distinguish among the four candidate ports. Selecting one would be unsupported.

llm_alone.decision: commit not to one place (4 locations); reported as a set

score.why: truth not in the reported set
